solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Coastal road hard to find in mass of snow

indicators.note: the letter for hard is to be found placed in the middle of the snow word

parts.note: a cornice is an overhanging mass of snow on a ridge
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A clifftop road buried somewhere in a snowdrift is tricky to locate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to find in' puts H inside CORNICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A corniche is a road cut along a cliff or coast, such as those on the Riviera.

clue.text: Persian ass runs on time to come first

indicators.note: the words before this phrase are placed ahead of the letter for runs

parts.note: an age is a period of time
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A Persian donkey keeps running in good time to win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs' is not the verb but the cricket scorer's R.
explanation.definitionFit: The onager is a wild ass native to Iran and nearby lands.

clue.text: Promotion splits Northern Irish, making deep point

indicators.note: the promotion word goes between the two abbreviations, splitting them

parts.note: an ad promotes a product

explanation.surface: A promotion divides people in Northern Ireland, making a profound point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Northern Irish' looks like one idea but gives two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point, as of fortunes or of the sky below an observer.

clue.text: Agreement to involve government statisticians in count

indicators.note: to involve something is to draw it in, so the statisticians go inside
in confirms the statisticians' letters sit within the count

parts.note: a census is an official count of population
ONS is the UK Office for National Statistics

explanation.surface: An agreement to bring official statisticians into the national count.
explanation.walkthrough: The ONS is Britain's Office for National Statistics, the body that runs the national count.
explanation.definitionFit: Consensus is general agreement among a group.

clue.text: Ready with foil, almost completed wrapping cloth up

indicators.note: wrapping means one piece goes round the other
almost means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: ended means completed

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a rag is a piece of cloth

explanation.surface: Kitchen foil is nearly finished after wrapping a cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' leaves ENDE; 'up' gives GAR, as this is a down clue. 'foil' is the fencing sword, not kitchen wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: En garde is the fencer's call to take a guard position, ready to fence with the foil.

clue.text: More subtle to invest 1,000 pounds?

definitions.note: the slang word for a pound sterling is the same in singular and plural

indicators.note: to invest here means to surround or besiege, so the thousand goes inside

parts.note: nicer can mean more finely discriminating, as in a nice distinction
K stands for a thousand, as in 10K

explanation.surface: Is it a cleverer move to put a thousand pounds into something?
explanation.walkthrough: 'to invest' puts K inside NICER. 'More subtle' uses nice in its old sense of precise. Nicker is British slang for a pound sterling.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicker is British slang for a pound sterling, used unchanged for several pounds, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Man-at-arms announced time to retire

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: a knight is a mounted soldier, a man-at-arms

explanation.surface: A soldier declares it is time to retire from service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retire' means go to bed, not stop working.
explanation.definitionFit: Night is when people go to bed, the time to retire for sleep.

clue.text: Ordered scones for King Edward?

indicators.note: ordered means arranged in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone ordered scones for a king called Edward, or for a potato variety.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward is also a British potato variety, which fits the scones surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward the Confessor was an English king, so his title is one example of the definition.

clue.text: What some observed about Estella's lover is revelation

indicators.note: the exclamation is seen placed about the lover's name, enclosing it

parts.note: eh is a query meaning what
Pip loves Estella in Dickens's Great Expectations
any can mean some, as in have you any

explanation.surface: Something certain people celebrated about Estella's admirer comes as a revelation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What some observed' also hints at the feast of the Epiphany, which some Christians keep, a pleasing extra layer.
explanation.definitionFit: An epiphany is a sudden moment of insight or realisation.

clue.text: Caper cut and put on bacon cube

indicators.note: a word that is cut has lost its end, here its final letter

parts.note: a caper is a prank or lark
to don clothes is to put them on

explanation.surface: A prank was cut short and a show staged, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes K from LARK, giving LAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A lardon is a small strip or cube of bacon or pork fat used in cooking.

clue.text: Concert, absurd performance, extremely great

parts.note: a gig is a live music performance
an antic is a grotesque or absurd act

explanation.surface: A review: the concert was a ridiculous show, extremely great.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' looks like an instruction to take outer letters, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something gigantic is huge, of enormous size, so extremely great.

clue.text: I concur that woman must catch a bird

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it within, so the pronoun wraps the other letters

parts.note: her refers to that woman
the rhea is a large flightless South American bird

explanation.surface: Someone agrees that a woman ought to capture a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhea is a South American flightless bird, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a cry of agreement in Parliament and meetings, so it says I agree.

clue.text: Supporter tense — ambassador to produce champers?

definitions.note: champers here are things that chomp, i.e. grinders in a baby's mouth

parts.note: a golf tee supports the ball
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
HE is His Excellency, the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: A golfing ambassador seems to be producing champagne for a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'champers' looks like slang for champagne but is read as 'things that champ', which babies grow.
explanation.definitionFit: Babies cut their first teeth, the champers or chewers, when they go through this stage.

clue.text: Reformed miser now doctor

indicators.note: formed again in a new shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the present is now

explanation.surface: A former miser now works as a physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reformed' rearranges MISER to MISRE.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor figures is to falsify them, which is giving a false account.

clue.text: Upheaval as Merlot replaced with Medoc at first

indicators.note: replaced means put back in a different place, so these letters are rearranged
at first means only the opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: Uproar in a wine bar as Merlot is swapped for Medoc.
explanation.walkthrough: 'replaced' rearranges AS and MERLOT into MAELSTRO.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a whirlpool and, by extension, a scene of violent turmoil.

clue.text: Start to read publication that includes new version

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
includes means holds within, so the letter for new goes inside

parts.note: an edition is an issue of a publication

explanation.surface: Begin reading a publication containing a fresh version of a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that includes' puts N inside EDITION.
explanation.definitionFit: A rendition is a performance or interpretation, one version of a piece.

clue.text: Soldiers needing minute to enter inviolate spacetime shortcut

indicators.note: enter means go inside, so these letters sit within the other word

parts.note: whole means intact, inviolate
OR stands for other ranks, i.e. soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops need a minute to break into a sealed shortcut through spacetime.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is 'other ranks', the army's term for soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: A wormhole is a theoretical tunnel through spacetime linking distant points.

clue.text: Change bowler is highly successful performer

parts.note: change is coins, i.e. money
a spinner is a cricket bowler who spins the ball

explanation.surface: A cricket captain's switch of bowler turns out to be an inspired one.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a spinner is a bowler who imparts spin; 'Change bowler' sounds like a captain's bowling change.
explanation.definitionFit: A money-spinner is something that earns a lot of cash, a lucrative product or venture.

clue.text: Sovereign, having dismissed army's leader, put in danger

indicators.note: dismissed means sent away, so a letter is removed

parts.note: imperial means sovereign, of an emperor

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter

explanation.surface: A monarch sacks the head of the army and puts him in danger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having dismissed' removes A, from 'army's leader', from IMPERIAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To imperil is to endanger, to expose to peril.

clue.text: Merchant of Venice's main scene?

parts.note: read as the setting where Venetian merchants did business, not the play's key scene

explanation.walkthrough: The clue points to Shakespeare's play, but asks for Venice's main commercial district; Shylock asks 'What news on the Rialto?'
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is the area of Venice where merchants traded, around its famous bridge.

clue.text: Adult thought caused a smile

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
to muse is to think

explanation.surface: A grown-up's reflection made someone grin.
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse someone is to entertain them so that they smile.

clue.text: Go with current meaning

definitions.meaning: to move along carried by water or air
the gist or sense of what is said

explanation.definitionFit: To drift is to be carried by a current; the drift of a remark is its general sense.

clue.text: Night-time habit regularly peeping into diary

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at even intervals, here every other one from the first

explanation.surface: Someone has a nightly custom of snooping in another's diary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habit' means a garment, not a custom.
explanation.definitionFit: A peignoir is a loose dressing gown or negligee, a garment worn at night.

clue.text: What one can make with hooter around?

definitions.text: What one can make with hooter around?

indicators.note: around means the nose word surrounds the letter for one

parts.note: hooter is slang for nose
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Someone using a car horn or a big nose makes a racket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooter' is slang for nose and also a car horn, which makes the whole clue a definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooter, whether horn or blown nose, produces a loud sound, a din.

clue.text: Messenger over time becomes royal attendant

indicators.note: the messenger lies over the time letter, covering it on both sides

parts.note: a courier carries messages

explanation.surface: A messenger is promoted over time to serve at court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' puts COURIER round T.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtier is someone who attends a monarch at court.

clue.text: Spot hook picked up for one to hang outside?

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the clue words are judged by their sound

parts.note: to spot something is to eye it; a sickle is a hooked reaping blade

explanation.surface: An instruction to notice a hook and lift it to hang outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one to hang outside?' is a cryptic definition: it hangs from the eaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Icicles form and hang from gutters and eaves outside in freezing weather.

clue.text: Protective wear brings endless assistance to London force

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: help is assistance
the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: Protective kit brings unending help to London's police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops P from HELP. The Met is the Metropolitan Police, London's force.
explanation.definitionFit: A helmet is headgear worn for protection, as by police officers.

clue.text: Knight takes look through narrow window

indicators.note: the word for look passes through, sitting in the middle of the window word

parts.note: a lancet is a tall narrow pointed window
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: A knight peers out through an arrow-slit window.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancelot is a famous Knight of the Round Table in Arthurian legend.
